PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 78 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 07/14/26 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, reassessment of fatigue, and ongoing management of anxiety and depressive symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for his follow-up appointment, primarily to evaluate the management of his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and the persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. He reports no significant change in his dyspnea, which continues to be exacerbated by physical activity and recent weather conditions. He acknowledges reliance on his albuterol inhaler, averaging eight to ten uses daily, particularly during episodes of increased humidity.
The bilateral lower extremity edema persists, with Mr. Fairfax adhering to dietary sodium restrictions and maintaining his furosemide regimen at 80 mg daily. He describes the edema as 1+ pitting, notably worsening after prolonged periods of ambulation. He denies any associated pain, warmth, or discoloration.
Mr. Fairfax continues to experience profound fatigue, which he characterizes as debilitating and limiting his engagement in daily activities. Additionally, he reports a slight increase in anxiety and depressive symptoms, particularly related to his health status and functional limitations.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + daytime dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, continued use at eight to ten times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 80 mg daily. 7. Sertraline 50 mg daily (ongoing management for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 80, BP 128/78, RR 24, O2 sat 82% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress but appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.0, Hgb 10.8, Hct 32.5, Plt 210 2. BMP: Na 132, K 4.1, Cl 95, CO2 23, BUN 28, Cr 1.7, Glucose 90 3. BNP: 650 (notable increase). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.6 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's dyspnea remains significant, and his reliance on albuterol has increased. A review of his inhaler technique was reinforced, and he was educated on the importance of adherence to prescribed inhaled corticosteroids. A referral to a pulmonary rehabilitation program is essential to improve his functional capacity and address his respiratory symptoms. Follow-up in 1 month for reassessment. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The persistent edema and further increase in creatinine levels necessitate additional evaluation. Dietary sodium restrictions should be reinforced, and Mr. Fairfax is encouraged to elevate his legs. A nephrology referral will be arranged for further evaluation given the increase in creatinine and worsening edema. 4. Fatigue and psychological well-being: Continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Given the exacerbation of fatigue and increased anxiety/depression, a follow-up appointment with a psychologist is crucial for ongoing support. Monitor CBC and metabolic panel in one month to assess for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
